quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When a traffic signal turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as fast as possible.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go through the intersection. But first, you must let pedestrians and other traffic that are still in the intersection cross or pass.

questions.question: Lanes going the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes going opposite directions.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down and let it pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You are in the right lane on a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter. Always use your signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Being physically fit does not change your BAC.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. But you must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt?
questions.explanation: The driver, front seat passengers, and all children under 16 must wear seat belts when the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: You see an animal on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.explanation: Always be very cautious around animals on the road. Pass them slowly so you don't scare them.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic
After stopping completely and checking that it is safe
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: After stopping completely and checking that it is safe
questions.explanation: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. Then proceed only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
You can drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells drivers that a traffic island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must keep to the right of it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Work is happening on the highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work is happening on the highway ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs are orange with black markings. They warn drivers about work zones ahead. Slow down and drive with extra care when you see this sign.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, night driving is:
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see in the dark. Headlights from other cars can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an open passing lane.
Even if it means driving off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an open passing lane.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right if there is an open passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at a four-way stop sign at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these is used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct turn lanes?

options.text: White lines on the edge of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign means pedestrians may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign do?

options.text: Warns drivers of hazards that exist or may happen.
Alerts drivers to food and gas nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns drivers of hazards that exist or may happen.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards that exist or may happen. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: Before turning left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Drive slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match highway traffic. Turn on your signal, find an opening, and merge safely.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: Stay and wait for the police.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
Leave and continue on your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find the owner, leave a written note on the car. Include your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Stop only if other cars are approaching.

questions.explanation: This sign shows a bicycle crossing or path. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles cross or ride near the road here.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the road edge. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a car on your right. You should:

options.text: Slow down and let the car on your right go.
Drive through and make the other car stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go.
questions.explanation: The vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Yield and let it pass first.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first since traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right. Finally, look left again to make sure nothing new is coming.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.

questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet makes roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit for safety.

questions.question: Which is not a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: If an oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.explanation: Honk to get attention. If the other driver does not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left—if the other driver corrects, you will still crash. Brake firmly. Losing speed reduces the impact.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, what should drivers do?

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.
Stop in the middle of the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection without traffic lights. Traffic flows counterclockwise around a center island. When entering, yield to any cars already in the roundabout, then follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road may become wet and slippery, so you should drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a roundabout is coming. Slow down as you enter and yield to any traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink any alcohol in a vehicle on a public road or sidewalk. You also cannot keep an open alcohol container in the front seat or anywhere the driver can reach it.

questions.question: What does an octagonal (8-sided) sign always mean?
questions.explanation: Every octagonal sign is a stop sign. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, 8-sided sign.

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way when a funeral procession is on the road?
questions.explanation: All drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to a funeral procession. Once the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the rest of the procession can follow through, even if the traffic light says stop.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: What does it mean when a driver extends their left arm straight up?
questions.explanation: When a driver raises their left arm upward, they are signaling that they plan to turn right. Adjust your driving if you see this signal.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Look for other vehicles that might also be moving into your lane. Never use your phone while driving.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Never make a sudden turn if you miss your exit. Continue to the next exit instead.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
Honk your horn and pass the bus on the left side.
Keep driving when you think the children have finished getting off.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm out. Do not move forward until the stop arm is put away.

questions.question: What can you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with enough tread.
Fill your tires to the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, your tires need good tread and the correct air pressure. You should also slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop right away and back up.
Driving conditions are not normal or safe.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not normal or safe.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: How should you prepare to handle hazards on the road ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and the sides of the road at all times.
Look straight ahead without moving your eyes.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Look only at the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and the sides of the road at all times.
questions.explanation: You can handle dangerous situations better if you see problems before you reach them. Look ahead, but also scan the sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: Anytime you turn on your emergency flashers.
If your vehicle is not touching the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only when you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: The traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, go through carefully.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, go through carefully.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before the intersection if it is safe. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield to?

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. You must also always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?

options.text: Do not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to pass safely. Only pass if you can do so safely and legally.

questions.question: You hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right side and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, make space for it and stop. Slow down and safely move to the side of the road. If traffic is heavy and the vehicle is directly behind you, keep moving slowly until you can get out of its way.
